- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model may lag; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion rule: if 3-day avg is >10% above recent 10-day avg, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to overestimate if sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply 1–2% downward bias if sentiment avg <0.50 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for next 3–5 days to avoid underestimating rebound.
